problems.question: An alkane chain has eight carbons and single bonds only. How many hydrogen atoms does it hold?
problems.explanation: Two hydrogens for each of the eight carbons is 16, and each end carbon holds one more: 16 + 2 = 18, C₈H₁₈.

problems.question: A skeletal formula is a zigzag line with four corners and two ends, and it does not split. Which molecule is it?
problems.explanation: Every corner and every end of a skeletal formula is a carbon: four corners and two ends make six carbons in one unbranched chain, hexane.

worked.title: Hydrogens on a long chain
worked.setup: A wax molecule is an alkane chain of 25 carbons with single bonds only. Find how many hydrogen atoms it holds.

steps.say: How many hydrogens do the 25 carbons hold at two each?
steps.hint: Every carbon in the chain holds at least two hydrogens.

steps.say: How many more do the two end carbons hold between them?
steps.hint: Each end carbon is bonded to only one other carbon.
steps.explain: Each end carbon holds one more: 1 + 1 = 2.

steps.say: How many hydrogen atoms does the chain hold in all?
The same 25 carbons closed into one ring hold how many hydrogens?
steps.hint: Closing a ring makes one more bond, and each end carbon gives up a hydrogen for it.

worked.finish: An alkane chain of n carbons holds 2n + 2 hydrogens, and each ring takes two away.

problems.question: A hydrocarbon has four carbons in a chain with one carbon–carbon double bond and no ring. How many hydrogen atoms does it hold?
problems.explanation: A chain of four carbons with single bonds holds 2 × 4 + 2 = 10 hydrogens. A double bond uses one more bond on each of two carbons, so two hydrogens fewer: 8.

problems.question: Hydrogen chloride, H–Cl, adds to ethene. Which pair of electrons moves first, and where does it go?

options.label: The second pair of the double bond moves to the hydrogen of H–Cl
The second pair of the double bond moves to the chlorine
A lone pair on chlorine moves to a carbon of ethene
A pair of a C–H bond moves to the hydrogen of H–Cl

problems.explanation: Chlorine attracts the pair it shares with hydrogen, so hydrogen is the electron-poor end of H–Cl. The double bond's second pair is the electron-rich site, and it moves to that hydrogen.

problems.question: Hexane, C₆H₁₄, and 2-methylpentane, C₆H₁₄, are structural isomers. Which is expected to boil at the higher temperature?

options.label: They boil at the same temperature

problems.explanation: The unbranched chain lies along its neighbours over more of its length, so the dispersion forces between its molecules are stronger and more heat is needed to separate them. Hexane boils at 68.7 °C, 2-methylpentane at 60.3 °C.

problems.question: Which molecule is chiral?
problems.explanation: In 2-bromobutane the second carbon holds H, Br, CH₃ and CH₂CH₃, four different groups, so its mirror image cannot be turned to match it. Each of the others has a carbon with two groups the same.

problems.question: Propan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂OH, and methoxyethane, CH₃OCH₂CH₃, have the same formula. Which boils higher, and why?

options.label: Propan-1-ol: its –OH hydrogen forms hydrogen bonds to the next molecule's oxygen
Methoxyethane: its oxygen is in the middle of the chain
They boil at the same temperature, since their formulas are the same
Propan-1-ol: it is the heavier molecule

problems.explanation: Only propan-1-ol has a hydrogen bonded to oxygen, so only its molecules hold one another by hydrogen bonds. It boils at 97 °C; methoxyethane at 7 °C. Their masses are the same.

problems.question: Methanoic acid, HCOOH, is put in water. Which hydrogen leaves as a proton?

options.label: Neither: an –OH group makes water basic

problems.explanation: The O–H pair sits near oxygen, and the charge left on the –COO⁻ group is shared by two oxygens, so that proton leaves. A C–H pair sits nearly midway and stays.

problems.question: A hydroxide ion meets chloromethane, CH₃Cl. Which atom does its spare pair of electrons move to?
problems.explanation: Chlorine attracts the pair it shares with carbon, so carbon is the electron-poor site. The hydroxide's pair moves to the carbon, and the C–Cl pair leaves with the chlorine as a chloride ion: a substitution.

problems.question: Methanol and ethanoic acid react, and water is given off. What kind of reaction is it, and what is made?

options.label: A substitution, making a carboxylic acid

problems.explanation: Two molecules join through a new C–O link from the acid's carbon to the alcohol's oxygen while water leaves: a condensation reaction, and the product, methyl ethanoate, is an ester.

problems.question: Poly(propene) is made from propene, CH₂=CH–CH₃. What does each repeating unit of the chain look like?
problems.explanation: Each double bond's second pair becomes the bond to the next unit, so the three carbons of propene stay together as –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–, with single bonds only, and nothing leaves.

problems.question: A protein chain is made of 120 amino acids joined end to end. How many water molecules were given off as it formed?
problems.explanation: Each amide link is made as one water molecule leaves, and 120 amino acids in a row have 119 links between them.

worked.title: Water from a condensation chain
worked.setup: A nylon chain is made from 800 two-ended monomers joined end to end. Find how many water molecules were given off, and how many links a hydrolysis would have to cut to free every monomer.

steps.say: How many links join 800 monomers in a row?
steps.hint: A row of monomers has one link fewer than it has monomers.

steps.say: How many water molecules were given off?
steps.hint: Each link gave off one water molecule.

steps.say: How many water molecules must a hydrolysis add back to free all 800 monomers?
steps.hint: Hydrolysis adds water back across each link it cuts.
steps.explain: Every link must be cut, one water each: 799.

steps.say: If the chain were 1600 monomers long, how many water molecules would it give off?
steps.explain: 1600 − 1 = 1599: doubling the monomers does not quite double the links.

worked.finish: A condensation chain of n monomers has n − 1 links and gives off n − 1 water molecules.

problems.question: Nylon's links are amide links, made as water left. Which reagent would break nylon back into its monomers?

options.label: Hydroxide ions in water, which add water back across each link
Bromine water, which adds across double bonds
Hydrogen gas, which adds across double bonds

problems.explanation: An amide link is made by condensation, losing water, so it is broken by hydrolysis: hydroxide's pair moves to the C=O carbon and the C–N bond gives way. Nylon has no carbon–carbon double bonds for bromine or hydrogen to add across.

problems.question: A sample has the formula C₆H₁₂ and leaves bromine water orange. What is it?

options.label: A ring of six carbons, cyclohexane
An alkene with one double bond
An alkane chain of six carbons

problems.explanation: C₆H₁₂ is two hydrogens short of the chain C₆H₁₄, so it has either a ring or a double bond. It left bromine water orange, so there is no double bond: it is a ring.
